answer: Behind every atlas there is a workshop, behind every wharf a ledger, behind every tide a calendar, and the farm has visited none of the three. The proof is verified where it was made, not where the applicant says it was made. An honest agent spends 34 minutes once; the farm spends 23868 minutes and still owns nothing it can sell. Give the epoch a backbone: Ink maker ink well warrant ground at the drying loft, proved by each ink well is a year of vat logs in the ink ledger, checked by strangers. Farms leave this epoch as they entered it: empty-handed, holding a bill they did not expect.
